newsitem.title: MEXICO: Yasuda to expand into financial services.
newsitem.headline: Yasuda to expand into financial services.

text.p: MEXICO CITY, July 14, Reuter - Yasuda Fire & Marine Insurance Co Ltd plans to begin offering life insurance and other financial service products as it moves to respond to growing competition from banks, its president said Monday.

Koichi Ariyoshi, speaking to Reuters in an interview at an International Insurance Society conference in Mexico City, said some of the new products could include pension, medical and unemployment insurance in addition to life insurance.
Insurance products for the elderly also are under consideration, he said.

Although competition from banks and other financial service companies has triggered massive consolidation in the U.S. insurance market, Ariyoshi said he did not foresee a similar scenario in Japan within the next few years. He said he did not believe Japanese companies would be able to achieve the cost savings necessary to make such acquisitions attractive.
In addition, many Japanese insurers have liabilities on their books that would make them unattractive takeover targets.

Even so, he said, such transactions may be just a matter of time. Indeed, Japan recently liberalized its holding company laws and is now discussing the details for the financial services industry, Ariyoshi said.

Until now, he said, holding companies had been prohibited. But with the details relating to the financial service sector still not finalized, he said he had no interest in any new arrangement for Yasuda, especially in connection with Fuji Bank Group.
"However, if conditions changed or if the holding company regulations and law involved become clear, theoretically speaking, there might be (interest)," he said through an interpreter.
Meanwhile, actual takeover interest may be more likely to come from outside of Japan.

"Foreign insurance companies seem to have a great deal of interest in acquiring Japanese insurance companies, Ariyoshi said after speaking with other participants at the conference Monday at the Camino Real hotel.
"I thought, today, in the near future maybe some foreign company could purchase a Japanese company," he said.
But foreign companies are likely to find many Japanese companies strongly opposed to the concept of foreign ownership, he said.
But, he said, "I think that kind of feeling is going to diminish" as Japanese companies themselves expand outside of their own country.
Meanwhile, Ariyoshi said he expected competition in Japan's insurance market to intensify next year following the country's deregulation of premium rates.
He said he expected rates to fall after the July deregulation and said companies that do not have a strong financial position would suffer.
Japanese insurers, he said, will be forced to strengthen their financial positions and reduce management costs.
For Yasuda, he said, the company planned to closely monitor the pricing, product offerings and services offered by competitors so that it can be quick to respond to new trends.
